Visual representation of property assets, equipment, and systems.
Learn the basics of documenting your property with Mapstead.
Mapstead is designed to help you organize and find everything important about your property. Follow these basic steps to get started:
Add a Property Map for your land or buildings.
Map your first building, boundary, utility, or spot.
Add System Items and link them to your map.
Add maintenance records and set reminders.
Add photos and documents for reference.
Manage property details, documents, and reports.

A Property is the main place where Mapstead organizes your information. It represents a single physical location, such as your home, a farm, a workshop, or a rental. It stores basic details and serves as the container for all maps, equipment records, and files.

A Property location is optional, but confirming one allows Mapstead to automatically create your first Property Map. You can always add a location or more Maps later. Locations and measurements are approximate and for reference only.

All working data is stored locally on this device. Mapstead is not a survey or legal boundary source. You should create periodic backups to stay safe. Files you export or share are outside of Mapstead\'s local storage.
Understand how maps, layers, and items work together.

Property Maps provide a visual reference for your land. You can create multiple Maps for a single property to show different details, such as outdoor utilities on one Map and building layouts on another.

Basemaps provide the background imagery. Detail varies by provider and location; some areas may show building footprints while others do not. You can outline your own structures using the mapping tools.
Learn how to map locations, routes, and areas.
Locations mark a single spot (well heads, valves). Routes trace lines (fences, pipes, paths). Areas outline structures or regions (houses, gardens, boundaries).
Presets like \"Well\" or \"Fence\" prefill the category and styling for you. Use \"Custom\" actions at the end of each category to map items not listed in the presets.
Tips for using phone GPS and understanding the accuracy circle.
Phone GPS is approximate and can be affected by weather, tree cover, and nearby buildings. The blue circle shows the estimated area where your device is located.
If your GPS signal is weak, use \"Tap the Map\" as an alternative. This allows you to place items precisely based on visual landmarks in the background map.
Organize your map by grouping related items.
Layers keep your map organized. You can hide layers to reduce clutter, or lock them to prevent accidental changes. You can also change a layer\'s opacity to see through filled areas.
New maps can start with standard layers like \"Buildings\", \"Utilities\", and \"Safety\" to help you categorize items from the beginning.
Keep detailed records of your equipment and systems.
System Items are detailed records for things like pumps, panels, or appliances. They store model numbers, service history, and instructions.
You can link a mapped feature to a System Item. This allows you to tap an item on the map and jump directly to its detailed service records.
Use Connections to show how systems relate. For example, a well pump might be \"Connected To\" a pressure tank. You can also define \"Feeds\" or \"Controls\" relationships.
Organize receipts, manuals, and property photos.
Photos and documents are managed locally. If you delete or move a file on your device outside of the app, Mapstead will show a warning that the file is missing.
Quickly find safety and utility shut-off information.
Emergency Mode highlights items you\'ve marked as critical, such as gas shut-offs or fire extinguishers. It provides immediate access to their location and instructions.
Emergency Mode depends on the accuracy of the data you enter. It does not contact emergency services automatically.
Create a PDF summary of your property records. Use the Handoff feature to bundle reports and all original photos/files into a single ZIP archive for sharing.
Switch between Imperial and Metric units.
Mapstead supports both Imperial (feet, acres) and Metric (meters, hectares) units. You can change this anytime in Settings.
Current status of data protection features.

Backup and restore is currently unavailable in customer builds while destructive restore testing is completed. Development builds use a ZIP-based format with SHA-256 integrity checks. Google Drive backup is not currently active.

Mapstead maps, measurements, GPS locations, property boundaries, and building outlines are approximate and intended for documentation and reference only. They are not a land survey, title record, utility locate, or legally binding boundary determination. Do not rely on them for construction, excavation, permitting, legal disputes, or safety-critical work. Verify important locations and boundaries with a licensed surveyor, utility-locate service, or other qualified professional.

Mapstead does not contact or replace emergency services. It does not replace a professional inspection. Customer-entered information may be incomplete, inaccurate, or outdated. Unmapped utilities and hazards may exist. Follow applicable utility-locate requirements before excavation.

Set up device notifications for recurring tasks.
If you grant the necessary permission, Mapstead can send you a notification when a maintenance task is due. Reminders can be linked to specific systems like filters or pumps.
If you prefer not to receive alerts on your device, you can still save reminders. They will be highlighted in the maintenance hub when they are due or overdue.
Track service history and keep a log of all work performed.
Document maintenance by recording the service date, provider, and cost. You can attach photos of the work or copies of receipts to keep all records in one place.
When adding a record, you can set an optional next due date. This helps you track upcoming tasks without setting up formal notifications.
Mapstead is designed as an offline-first application. All property details, equipment records, and maintenance logs are stored locally on your device\'s internal storage.

Photos and documents you attach to property items remain on your device. Mapstead manages these files in its private data directory. If you delete an attachment in the app, the local file is also removed.

Current customer builds of Mapstead do not perform automatic cloud synchronization. Your data is not uploaded to our servers. Backup functionality, when enabled, uses your own personal cloud storage (such as Google Drive) and is under your control.

Mapstead uses Internet access to download online basemap tiles and other map-provider content. Current customer builds do not automatically synchronize your property database or upload it to Mapstead servers.
Mapstead requests foreground location access when you choose a location feature, such as centering the map or placing an item using phone GPS.
Mapstead may request notification permission when you enable maintenance reminders.
Mapstead uses Android’s system photo, document, camera, and sharing interfaces. Selected files are copied into app-managed local storage.
When you use the \'Property Handoff\' or \'PDF Report\' features, Mapstead generates files for you to share. You have full control over who receives these files through the Android share system.
Removing a property hides it from normal use by marking it deleted. Related records and app-managed files may remain until dedicated cleanup or permanent-deletion support is applied.
